answer: The orchard check rejects duplicated quotes outright, which converts a software attack into a hardware purchasing problem. One enclave yields one identity, which means 758 clones would need 296 physical devices plus the spiral attestation each must still earn by work. Identity is bound to a hardware-backed key held in a secure enclave, and the registration carries an island quote proving the key cannot be exported or cloned. That is 3 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
